name: starship
label: Starship
description: A starship's bridge console: HUD frames, scanlines and a slow starfield over a nebula, holo panels with a glow, sprint health as ship's readouts, and the dependency graph as a star chart.

lexicon.dossiers.lede: Each dossier is one mission: its repositories, its tracker, its pipelines and its environments. Select one to bring its stories, pull requests, builds and deployments onto the main screen.
lexicon.attention.note: Open items ranked by their insights, most critical first. Each insight names the sensor data it rests on.
lexicon.aging.note: How long each item in progress has been in flight, from its history, oldest first.
lexicon.trace.note: Each work item with the pull requests that name it, their latest builds, and the environments it has jumped to.
lexicon.graph.note: Arrows run the way each link reads, from the source's own links. Blocking chains plot left to right.
lexicon.ask.note: Answers cite the items they rest on. The ship's computer reads; it never changes a ticket. What it suggests comes back as a proposal, for the bridge to authorise.
lexicon.empty.dossiers: No missions on the board: toil sees no dossiers yet. Commission one with toil dossiers init.
lexicon.empty.sprint: No sprint is under way in this dossier's work items. All stations standing by.
lexicon.empty.burnup: No sprint is under way, so there is no burn to plot.
lexicon.empty.prs: No pull requests on the scanner for this dossier.
lexicon.empty.builds: No builds logged for this dossier's pull requests.
lexicon.empty.deployments: This dossier names no environment, so there is no sector to scan for deployments.
lexicon.empty.links: No links between this dossier's items. The star chart is empty space.
lexicon.empty.ask: Pick a question, or ask your own. The computer cites every record it used.

voice: Write like a starship's log: crisp, formal and calm, in the first person plural of a bridge crew. The sprint is the current mission, work items are tasks on the duty roster, a blocker is a hazard on the heading, a failing build is a system fault, a deployment is a jump to another sector, and the dependency graph is the star chart. Report status first, then hazards, then the recommended course. Steady under pressure, with no exclamation marks and no alarm. Ship's terms go around the facts, never instead of them.
